Maya Li: Heads-up — onboarding the new open-7B-int4-v2 model for long-context benchmarks and seeing divergence after ~6.5k tokens on our RoPE-enabled tests. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Rob Patel: ugh ok thanks for flagging. Is this only on int4 or also float16?

Maya Li: only on int4 so far. float16 baseline looks fine up to 16k in our quick runs. I can paste minimal repro.

Cheng Wu: can you add the exact run command + seed? also which rotary scaling variant? scaled or fused?

Maya Li: running with --rope-mode=scaled --rope-alpha=1.0 (default). Command: `./run_eval.sh --model open-7b-int4-v2 --ctx 8192 --quant int4 --rope scaled --seed 42 --profile kv`

Maya Li: result snippet: `loss diverged after step 120 (token 6523), topk probs shifted, repeated phrase injected`

Rob Patel: hmm repeated phrase + drift -> smells like kv cache mis-indexing or wrap offset when quantized. Did you enable the KVCACHE_PREFILL flag?

Maya Li: yes prefill enabled. switching it off makes behavior different (slower but no immediate drift). Also noticed slight mismatch in kv indexes when dumping keys.

Sophie Gonzales: quick idea: int4 packing changed data alignment -> memcpy path in prefill might be doing unaligned moves on some GPU kernels. We saw a similar pattern on magnet13b onboarding. Can you dump `kv_indices` and `rotary_offsets` for the failing batch?

Maya Li: attaching short dump (pasted): `KV_IDX: [0,1,2,...,6522,6523,6523,6523]` — looks like repeats at the tail. Rotary offsets show wrap at 4096 but tokens >4096 are expected.

Cheng Wu: if KV_IDX repeats the tail that's probably an eviction boundary being applied incorrectly during a prefill->inflight merge. Which shard mode? single-shard or interleaved?

Maya Li: interleaved. We recently changed shard handshake to use compact indices for int4 to save memory. Could be related.

Rob Patel: try forcing `SHARD_MODE=single` on that run to see if reproducible. If it's gone, we know it's an interleaving/packing regression. Also run with `--rope-alpha=0.5` to test sensitivity.

Maya Li: repro matrix started: int4/interleaved/scaled/alpha1.0 -> fail; int4/single/scaled/alpha1.0 -> fail sometimes; float16/interleaved/scaled -> pass; int4/interleaved/scaled/alpha0.5 -> reduces incidence but still rare.

Sophie Gonzales: ok that partial reduction suggests rotary amplitude interacts with quant noise. Two-pronged: 1) add assert on kv idx monotonicity at merge points; 2) disable compact-index packing temporarily.

Maya Li: adding assert now. quick log: `kv_merge_assert FAILED at merge_idx 6523: prev_idx=6522 cur_idx=6523 next_idx=6523` -> shows duplicate target index.

Cheng Wu: interesting — where is the compact pack applied? in `prefill_pack_indices()` in prefill_kv.cu or during the shard handshake?

Maya Li: in prefill_kv.cu before RPC send. I added a debug build (no quant pack) and the failure disappears for 100+/100 runs.

Rob Patel: so likely bug in packing code for int4 where two tokens map to the same compact slot when sequence > radix boundary. Could be off-by-one in stride calculation.

Sophie Gonzales: can we roll a microfix: change packing stride to be ceil(seq / words_per_pack) instead of floor? Add unit test that simulates non-even division for anchor strides.

Maya Li: trying microfix patch now in branch `fix/int4-pack-stride`. Running 200-run smoke with ctx=8192.

qa-bot: test-run started by Maya Li — 200 randomized seeds, ctx=8192, model=open-7b-int4-v2, run_id=qa-5123456789-1

Maya Li: quick update — after microfix initial 200-run: 200/200 passes, no kv-index duplicates, no phrase repeats seen in sample traces.

Rob Patel: nice! can you push the change to a gated MR and add the new unit test and a small perf check? we should validate no perf regression from packing change.

Maya Li: will do. perf quick: packing overhead down ~+0.2% CPU, no token latency change on p99. I'll add the MR notes about risk and test coverage.

Sophie Gonzales: also schedule a longer soak (24h) across dedicated pools with different sequence distributions — some workloads have long bursts that stress packing.

Maya Li: scheduling soak. thanks all. tagging @eng-platform to watch for any rollout issues. :rocket:

Rob Patel: great root cause isolation — excellent triage team work. :tada:

qa-bot: MR created: https://git.internal/redwood/rlib/pull/4821 — CI: unit tests passed (3/3), smoke 200/200 passed, perf check nominal

Maya Li: merging after CI, will monitor metrics on next deploy to staging. Closing thread unless someone wants to keep discussing followups.

Sophie Gonzales: please file postmortem-lite in /incidents if any customer impact later.

Maya Li: will file notes in docs.
